newsitem.title: TAIWAN: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - May 2.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Taiwan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
CHINA TIMES - Taiwan presidential office urges Beijing to sign "peace accord".
President Lee Teng-hui pays respect to Pai Hsiao-yen, daughter of renowned actress Pai Ping-ping.
UNITED DAILY NEWS - Police continue search for killers of Pai Hsiao-yen.
Southern Chiayi county council chairman Hsiao Teng-piao, wanted by police for suspected links with underworld, emerges from 130-day disappearance to host council meeting.
LIBERTY TIMES - Hsiao Teng-piao denies involvement with gangsters.
Police detain fourth suspect in murder of Pai Hsiao-yen.
COMMERCIAL TIMES - Lee Kao-chao, vice chairman of Council for Economic Planning and Development, says Taiwan's bullish economic indicators in March may not reflect reality.
Taiwan workers stage street protest to demand more rights and benefits.
ECONOMIC DAILY NEWS - Talks on shipping links between Taiwan and Hong Kong after British colony's handover to Beijing may not yield immediate solution.
United States demands that Taiwan lower tariffs on car parts during talk on Taipei's entry into World Trade Organisation.
